sarah: quick q before tonight's window — what's our public policy for semver bumping on docs-only or metadata-only releases? do we bump patch or leave the tag?

matt: short answer: if the published artifact changes (docker npm dist etc) we should bump. even docs-only that go into the same release artifact -> patch.

jen: can we define 'published artifact' explicitly? if we only update a markdown in the repo but don't publish a new package, then no bump. but if the CI produces a new build (even identical code + new docs file) it counts.

olivia: +1 to jen. Practically we've had confusion when a docs push triggered a new image build and then people couldn't tell if it's safe to skip a patch bump.

sam: counterpoint: bumping patch for pure docs bloats release history. can we instead use build metadata? e.g. `1.2.3+docs.20260320` so semver precedence stays same but we record it.

kai: that's clever but build metadata is ignored by most package managers and tags. git tags with `+` are legal but some registries don't like them. also release tooling (changelogs, publish pipelines) don't always surface build metadata.

matt: true. we ran into that with the npm registry and `+` in tags. We need something that works end-to-end.

jen: proposal (practical):

```
- code changes (api/behavior) -> bump according to semver (major/minor/patch)
- packaging/infra changes -> bump patch
- docs-only that produce a new published artifact (image/npm) -> bump patch
- docs-only that do NOT produce a new published artifact -> no bump, but add changelog entry
- rollback-only metadata edits (e.g., fix release notes) -> don't bump; instead append a signed git tag `rollback/<orig-tag>` and push a small patch release only if artifact changes
```

olivia: I like that. It keeps semantic meaning and avoids weird `+` metadata.

oncall-sre: reminder — if this goes into tonight's change window (02:00 UTC), any patch bump will cause our release bots to deploy images to staging and production. we need release notes and a canary.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: 2026-03-20 02:00 UTC for tag `v1.12.5` -> staging -> canary. Use `--canary=5%`.

sarah: question about rollbacks: if we deploy v1.12.5 and rollback because of a non-code issue (e.g., bad release notes causing customer confusion) do we create v1.12.6 to re-release the previous artifact, or reuse v1.12.4?

matt: if rollback is to a previous artifact, we should re-release the previous validated artifact as a new patch (v1.12.6) instead of reusing old tags — avoids tag rewriting. tag rewriting is a no-go for published images.

sam: agree. example workflow:

```
- deploy v1.12.5
- detect issue unrelated to binary (docs/notes)
- rollback to v1.12.4 artifact
- create v1.12.6 pointing at the v1.12.4 artifact (changelog: rollback of v1.12.5 due to release-note regression)
```

kai: small nit: ensure the release author signs the rollback tag and we include `rollback-meta` labels so our billing/observability map shows the correct artifact origin.

olivia: also add a one-line note in the release body: `Rollback of v1.12.5 -> artifact v1.12.4; created v1.12.6` so search works.

jen: operational checklist for tonight (from policy):
- confirm whether docs change created a new artifact
- if yes -> bump patch and follow normal release flow
- if no -> push docs to main, add changelog entry, no version bump
- for any rollback -> never rewrite tags; create new patch release pointing to chosen artifact and mark it as rollback in release notes

sarah: awesome, I'll put this in the release playbook and add a short blurb in the PR template. tagging convention we'll standardize as `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` and rollback tags `rollback/vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-<short-sha>`.

matt: sounds good. @deploy-bot: please hold the staging deploy until changelog is confirmed.

deploy-bot: acknowledged — staging deploy paused. react with :thumbsup: when ready.

olivia: I'll add the changelog entry now and ping when done.

sarah: thanks all :rocket:
